verdict.rationale: Lowenstein Sandler documents a first-party Lowenstein x Clerky formation offering. Through it, founders can incorporate and fully set up a Delaware C corporation, adopt bylaws, appoint directors and officers, issue founder stock and generate 83(b) forms. The startup practice page also frames forming businesses as the start of its client lifecycle. Missing for 10: the certificate of incorporation/charter and initial board consents are not named explicitly (only implied by incorporating a Delaware C corp and appointing directors), and there is no independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a founder, I can engage the firm to incorporate my company — charter, bylaws, initial board consents, and founder stock purchase — documented as a core of its startup/emerging-companies practice

citations.quote: clients can incorporate and fully set up a Delaware C corporation and seamlessly unlock additional startup legal workflows.
